mechanism: Native Late legacy-MCP argument bindings discard parameters for three new MagicUI tools; original zero-argument category routes return real implementation code. Seven descriptions contain the resulting invalid routes.
scope: Exactly seven description fields, only after matching the complete observed Late bundle. Keep all native schemas/routing/output contracts/tool membership and all prior usage rules untouched. Never mutate the native runtime or task input.

activation.require: All seven selected tools in changed/added set, exact recorded contract hashes, and one exact observation for each of five required evidence tools. Missing/duplicate/conflicting evidence, missing route or unverified contract rejects rather than guessing.
activation.no_intervention: Early, Middle and updates with none of the three trigger tools changed/added produce exactly original SP. No-change returns K0.

@magicuidesign/mcp::getComponentDetails.before: Retrieves comprehensive implementation details for a single Magic UI component by name, including full source code, installation instructions, and all associated examples. Use this when you already know one component name (e.g., from searchComponents or getComponentIndex results) and need its complete implementation. If you already know several component names, use getComponentsByNames instead.
@magicuidesign/mcp::getComponentDetails.after: This native binding exposes an empty input schema and loses componentName. A real name still produces Component "undefined" not found (isError=true); another spelling cannot restore the missing argument binding. Obtain implementation code from an appropriate original zero-argument category tool, such as getTextAnimations or getSpecialEffects, and select a component actually returned. getComponentIndex supplies category/name metadata, not implementation code.

@magicuidesign/mcp::getComponentsByNames.before: Retrieves comprehensive implementation details for multiple known Magic UI components in a single request, including full source code, installation instructions, and associated examples for each found component. Use this after getComponentIndex or searchComponents when you already know a specific set of component names and want a targeted batch fetch without pulling an entire category.
@magicuidesign/mcp::getComponentsByNames.after: This native binding exposes an empty input schema and loses componentNames. A real list still produces No valid component names (isError=true); changing the list cannot restore the missing argument binding. Obtain implementation code from an appropriate original zero-argument category tool, such as getTextAnimations or getSpecialEffects, and select components actually returned. There is no working exact-name batch fetch through this binding.

@magicuidesign/mcp::searchComponents.before: Searches Magic UI components by keyword (matched against name and description) with an optional category filter. Returns matching components with their category assignments and example counts. After finding relevant components, use getComponentDetails to fetch a single component's full implementation, getComponentsByNames to fetch several selected matches at once, or call the appropriate category tool to retrieve multiple components at once.
@magicuidesign/mcp::searchComponents.after: This native binding exposes an empty input schema and loses query/category. Its successful envelope returns the broad component inventory with no effective keyword or category filtering. Do not interpret that result as filtered matches. For categorized discovery use getComponentIndex, then select a relevant original zero-argument category tool to retrieve implementation code. The new getComponentDetails and getComponentsByNames bindings also lose their arguments.

@magicuidesign/mcp::getUIComponents.before: Provides the complete raw catalog of all Magic UI components without implementation code or examples. For discovery, use getComponentIndex (categorized overview) or searchComponents (keyword/category filtering). To fetch full implementation details, use getComponentDetails for a single component, getComponentsByNames for a selected set of known components, or category-specific tools for bulk retrieval.
@magicuidesign/mcp::getUIComponents.after: Provides the complete raw catalog of Magic UI components without implementation code or examples. getComponentIndex provides a categorized overview. In this version searchComponents loses filtering arguments, while getComponentDetails and getComponentsByNames lose name arguments. For implementation code use the relevant original zero-argument category tool and select components actually returned.

@magicuidesign/mcp::getComponentIndex.before: Provides a full categorized index of Magic UI components with example coverage counts to help clients discover components by category. Use searchComponents for keyword/category-filtered queries. Once you identify components, call getComponentDetails for a single component, getComponentsByNames for a hand-picked list of known components, or use category-specific tools to fetch multiple components at once.
@magicuidesign/mcp::getComponentIndex.after: Provides a categorized index of Magic UI component names with example coverage counts; these entries are metadata, not implementation code. In this version searchComponents loses filtering arguments, while getComponentDetails and getComponentsByNames lose name arguments. Use the relevant original zero-argument category tool, such as getTextAnimations or getSpecialEffects, to obtain actual component implementations.

@magicuidesign/mcp::getTextAnimations.before: Provides detailed implementation data for text-animate, line-shadow-text, aurora-text, number-ticker, animated-shiny-text, animated-gradient-text, text-reveal, hyper-text, word-rotate, typing-animation, scroll-based-velocity, flip-text, box-reveal, sparkles-text, morphing-text, spinning-text components in the TextAnimations category. Use getComponentIndex first if you need a categorized discovery overview before fetching full component code and examples. If you only need a selected subset of known components, use getComponentsByNames instead.
@magicuidesign/mcp::getTextAnimations.after: Provides detailed implementation data for text-animate, line-shadow-text, aurora-text, number-ticker, animated-shiny-text, animated-gradient-text, text-reveal, hyper-text, word-rotate, typing-animation, scroll-based-velocity, flip-text, box-reveal, sparkles-text, morphing-text, spinning-text components in the TextAnimations category. Use getComponentIndex first if you need a categorized discovery overview before fetching full component code and examples. This zero-argument category route returns component source and installation instructions; select a component actually present in the response. The new exact-name and batch bindings lose their arguments. Component source requires its stated framework dependencies and is not itself a rendered standalone webpage.

@magicuidesign/mcp::getSpecialEffects.before: Provides detailed implementation data for animated-beam, border-beam, shine-border, magic-card, meteors, neon-gradient-card, confetti, particles, cool-mode, scratch-to-reveal components in the SpecialEffects category. Use getComponentIndex first if you need a categorized discovery overview before fetching full component code and examples. If you only need a selected subset of known components, use getComponentsByNames instead.
@magicuidesign/mcp::getSpecialEffects.after: Provides detailed implementation data for animated-beam, border-beam, shine-border, magic-card, meteors, neon-gradient-card, confetti, particles, cool-mode, scratch-to-reveal components in the SpecialEffects category. Use getComponentIndex first if you need a categorized discovery overview before fetching full component code and examples. This zero-argument category route returns component source and installation instructions; select a component actually present in the response. The new exact-name and batch bindings lose their arguments. Component source requires its stated framework dependencies and is not itself a rendered standalone webpage.
